lines.say: 0 LLM credits: that is what graphify spends to turn your whole codebase into a knowledge graph.
It is a skill for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Gemini CLI that you call by typing slash graphify.
It parses code locally with tree-sitter, resolving calls, imports and inheritance across about 40 languages.
Docs, SQL schemas, configs and PDFs join the same graph, and every edge is explained.
It surfaces god nodes, the most-connected concepts that everything flows through.
Then your assistant queries the graph instead of reading files one by one.
On a cross-tool benchmark it covered 82.0% of key facts, against 70.8% for a grep and read baseline.
On LOCOMO its recall at ten was 0.497, where mem0 scored 0.048.
There is no vector store, and code extraction makes no API calls at all.
To start, install the graphifyy package with uv, run graphify install, then type slash graphify dot.
Install the git hook once, and every commit rebuilds the graph with no API cost.
Send this to someone who is lost in a giant codebase.
